lines.text: Mini LED is not a new kind of screen.
Lift the picture off: it is still an LCD.
The new part is behind it, a grid of tiny lights.
They dim in zones, so the dark stays dark.
A zone is not a pixel: each one lights 6,400 pixels.
So before you buy, ask how many zones.

post.title: Mini LED is not a new kind of screen
post.caption:
"Mini LED" on a TV box is NOT a new kind of screen 📺

It is still an LCD. The new part is the light behind the picture: a grid of tiny LEDs that dim in zones, so dark parts of the picture stay dark.

Why now: TrendForce (16 Nov 2026) expects Mini LED TV shipments to reach 28.78 million in 2026, up 116% in a year, close to 15% of all TVs. You will see the label a lot this Black Friday.

But a zone is not a pixel. Apple's Studio Display XDR spec page lists 5120 x 2880 pixels (14.7 million) and a Mini-LED backlight with 2304 dimming zones. That works out to 6,400 pixels sharing each zone. Apple's own page says more precise zones mean deeper blacks and less halo.

So before you buy a Mini LED TV or monitor, ask one thing: how many dimming zones?

Did you know this? Yes or no 👇 Send this to the friend who is TV shopping this week.

sources.note: TrendForce, 16 Nov 2026, Global TV Shipments Decline 3.6% YoY in 3Q26 as Brands Target Premium Mini LED and RGB Mini LED Markets (read 24 Nov 2026): 'global Mini LED TV shipments will reach 28.78 million units in 2026, representing a remarkable 116% YoY increase and bringing market penetration close to 15%'; 'a broader shift in the premium LCD TV market. Competition is no longer centered solely on Mini LED backlight specifications and the number of local dimming zones' (Mini LED TVs are LCD TVs with a Mini LED backlight).

Apple, Studio Display XDR page (read 24 Nov 2026): '27-inch 5K Retina XDR display with mini-LED backlight'; '2304 dimming zones deliver remarkably precise lighting. For deeper blacks, brighter whites, and reduced halo and blooming.'

Apple, Studio Display XDR technical specifications (read 24 Nov 2026): '5120-by-2880 resolution at 218 pixels per inch'; 'Mini-LED backlight with 2304 dimming zones'. Our sum: 5120 x 2880 = 14,745,600 pixels; 14,745,600 / 2304 = 6,400 pixels per zone (64 x 36 zones of 80 x 80 pixels is our drawing of that sum; Apple does not state the zone layout).
